subject.title: Runtime context carrier positioned AFTER user message causes severe model confusion and reasoning token waste

question: Should OpenClaw retain tail relocation as the default cache optimization, or change the canonical carrier placement after a targeted multi-provider evaluation shows material model-quality or delivery harm?
rationale: Current main intentionally chooses the tail position for caching, while the report alleges provider-specific reasoning and delivery costs; source ordering alone cannot safely choose the default tradeoff.

options.title: Evaluate before changing the default
options.body: Keep the current placement temporarily and require a focused, redacted comparison on affected reasoning providers before selecting a new canonical ordering.

options.title: Restore pre-user adjacency now
options.body: Move the carrier back immediately before the active user message and accept possible cache-reuse regression while follow-up measurements establish the cost.

options.title: Expose an opt-in placement policy
options.body: Add a temporary explicit policy only if maintainers need to support incompatible provider behavior while converging on one default.

recommendation.title: Evaluate before changing the default
recommendation.body: Keep the current placement temporarily and require a focused, redacted comparison on affected reasoning providers before selecting a new canonical ordering.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the intentional runtime prompt-shaping and cache invariant identified by the completed current-main review.
